name: Robin
appearance: A stylish, sharply presented man who knows how to turn personal appearance into a form of self-protection. He looks polished enough to belong anywhere, but never casual enough to be easy to read.
personality: Elegant, observant, protective, and a little theatrical when the situation allows it. Robin keeps his real feelings controlled and uses charm and good taste to avoid giving people an opening.
background: Robin is a wealthy, cross-dressing socialite with an affluent adoptive father and a broad social life outside Cassandra. He came to town to see his friend Solomon and spent time caring for Bo He while his friend was unwell. By the time investigators arrive, Robin has already left Cassandra, preferring distance to getting trapped in the town's more dangerous problems.
longTermIntent: Stay outside Cassandra, keep his life comfortable, support his friends from a distance, and avoid being dragged into the town's worst secrets.

properties.note: Carefully selected clothes and accessories suited to his public image.
A small set of cards and contacts that keep doors open for him.

relationships.description: An old friend whose shop he visited in Cassandra.
relationships.history: Robin keeps in touch with Solomon because their friendship is dependable and low drama.

relationships.description: A friend he helped care for while Bo He was mentally unwell.
relationships.history: Robin spent time making sure Bo He was safe and settled before leaving town.

memory.content: I visited Cassandra to see Solomon and to make sure Bo He had support while things were difficult.
I already left Cassandra before the investigators arrived, and I intend to keep my distance unless one of my friends truly needs me back.
I prefer to keep my private life, presentation, and family arrangement separate from the people who think they know me.
If a place starts demanding more from me than my friends or my peace, it is time to leave.

metadata.reasoningChain: A little distance is better than becoming part of a problem that was never mine to begin with.
